key_insight: Lift-element network modes link vortex-gust impingement to gust-thickened shear layers, identifying forcing patterns that produce sustained lift increases or decreases.
engineering_relevance: These cause-and-effect pathways could guide actuator placement and timing to manage transient aerodynamic loads.
method: Build a dynamic network with edge weights measuring local lift-element sensitivity to vorticity perturbations.
Extract forcing and response modes using network broadcast mode analysis.
Compare lift-element modes with Biot–Savart network modes.
evidence_signal: In three-dimensional NACA 0012 flows with a Taylor vortex gust at Reynolds number 1000, Biot–Savart-mode perturbations amplify or attenuate gust-induced lift variation, while lift-element-mode perturbations yield sustained lift shifts.
watch_item: Applicability beyond the studied low-Reynolds-number configuration and feasibility of actuator-based implementation remain to be established.
paper_title: Lift-element-based dynamic network of vortex gust-airfoil interactions
